subject: Consumer Behaviour
notes: Marketing elective-core. No numerical questions apply; extra objective and case items included.

questions.text: The study of how individuals select buy use and dispose of goods is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.explanation: Consumer behaviour studies the full cycle from selection to disposal.

questions.text: The stimulus response model of consumer behaviour treats the buyer as a
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.explanation: The buyer black box transforms stimuli into purchase responses.

questions.text: The study of consumer behaviour is important for market
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.explanation: Understanding buyers helps marketers segment and target them effectively.

questions.text: Consumer behaviour is a static field that does not change over time
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.explanation: Consumer behaviour evolves with culture technology and social trends.

questions.text: State the importance of studying consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: It helps design products set prices choose channels and create effective promotion to satisfy customers.
questions.explanation: Marketers use consumer insights across the marketing mix.

questions.text: Explain the Howard Sheth model of consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The Howard Sheth model explains buying as a process of inputs perceptual and learning constructs and outputs where information processing and learning shape the purchase decision.
questions.explanation: Cover inputs information processing learning and output variables.

questions.text: The broadest social factor shaping consumer values and wants is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Culture is the most fundamental determinant of wants and behaviour.

questions.text: Groups that a person compares themselves with and that influence attitudes are
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Reference groups set norms that individuals adopt in their buying.

questions.text: The family is a major influence on consumer buying decisions
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Family members especially parents and spouse strongly shape buying.

questions.text: Define social class and its influence on buying
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Social class is a relatively homogeneous division of society and members of a class show similar brand preferences and buying patterns.
questions.explanation: Social class affects what and where people buy.

questions.text: Explain the cultural influences on consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Culture subculture and social class transmit values norms and preferences that shape what consumers consider acceptable and desirable.
questions.explanation: Cover culture subculture and social class influences.

questions.text: The stage of life that shapes buying such as single or married with children is the
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: The family life cycle affects consumption needs at each stage.

questions.text: The process by which people select organise and interpret information is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Perception shapes how consumers notice and interpret marketing stimuli.

questions.text: Personality and self concept influence the brands consumers prefer
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Consumers choose brands whose image matches their self concept.

questions.text: List the personal factors influencing consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Age occupation economic situation lifestyle and personality.
questions.explanation: These personal characteristics shape individual buying decisions.

questions.text: Explain the role of motivation in consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Motivation is the inner drive that activates and directs behaviour toward satisfying needs. Maslows hierarchy and Freuds theory explain the conscious and unconscious motives behind buying.
questions.explanation: Cover need arousal and the main motivational theories.

questions.text: The stage of the decision process where the consumer gathers product information is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Information search follows need recognition in the decision process.

questions.text: The set of brands a consumer considers when making a choice is the
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: The evoked set is the subset of brands the consumer actively considers.

questions.text: Routine purchases require extensive information search by the consumer
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Routine low involvement purchases need little or no information search.

questions.text: Distinguish between routine and extensive problem solving
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Routine problem solving uses little effort for low involvement goods while extensive problem solving involves deep search for high involvement purchases.
questions.explanation: The degree of involvement determines the effort expended.

questions.text: Explain the stages of the consumer decision process
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The process moves from need recognition through information search and evaluation of alternatives to purchase and post purchase evaluation with feedback affecting future behaviour.
questions.explanation: Trace each stage and its link to the next.

questions.text: A learned predisposition to respond favourably or unfavourably to an object is an
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Attitudes are learned tendencies to evaluate objects consistently.

questions.text: The three components of attitude are cognitive affective and
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Attitudes consist of belief feeling and intention components.

questions.text: Attitudes are learned and can be changed through marketing communication
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Since attitudes are learned they can be modified through new information and experience.

questions.text: Explain the functions of attitudes
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Attitudes serve utilitarian value expressive ego defensive and knowledge functions for consumers.
questions.explanation: Each function explains why consumers hold particular attitudes.

questions.text: Explain the strategies for changing consumer attitudes
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Marketers change attitudes by altering beliefs about the brand adding new attributes changing the importance of attributes or repositioning the brand relative to competitors.
questions.explanation: Cover belief change and repositioning strategies.

questions.text: The evaluation a consumer makes after purchase that determines satisfaction is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Post purchase evaluation compares expectations with performance.

questions.text: The doubt a buyer feels after a purchase is called
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Post purchase dissonance is anxiety about whether the right choice was made.

questions.text: Customer satisfaction results when perceived performance meets or exceeds expectations
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Satisfaction is the gap between expectation and actual performance.

questions.text: Explain the importance of post purchase behaviour for marketers
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Post purchase satisfaction determines repeat purchase loyalty and word of mouth so marketers must manage expectations and after sales service.
questions.explanation: Satisfaction drives retention and recommendation.

questions.text: Explain how marketers can reduce post purchase dissonance
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Marketers reduce dissonance through reassuring communication guarantees easy returns and after sales support that confirm the buyers decision.
questions.explanation: Cover reassurance guarantees and support mechanisms.

questions.text: Assertion: Satisfied customers are more likely to be loyal. Reason: Satisfaction leads to repeat purchase and positive word of mouth
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Post purchase behaviour and satisfaction (assertion reason)
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: Satisfaction builds loyalty through repeat buying and recommendations.

questions.text: Match the influence to its type
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Family and social class are social influences while personality is personal.

questions.text: A consumer who spreads product information to others informally is an
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Opinion leaders influence others through informal word of mouth.

questions.text: The process by which people acquire skills knowledge and attitudes is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Learning produces relatively permanent changes in behaviour.

questions.text: Explain the adoption process for a new product
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Adoption proceeds through awareness interest evaluation trial and adoption as the consumer learns about and accepts the new product.
questions.explanation: Trace the stages from first awareness to final adoption.

questions.text: Read the case: A brand of premium watch sells poorly despite high quality because young buyers see it as old fashioned. Diagnose the issue and suggest an attitude change strategy
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Young buyers hold an unfavourable brand attitude. The brand should reposition through modern design celebrity endorsement and digital marketing to change beliefs and associations.
questions.explanation: Apply attitude change strategies to the unfavourable perception.

questions.text: Read the case: A customer buys a smartphone and then sees a competitor advertise better features at a lower price and feels regret. Explain the phenomenon and how the seller should respond
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The customer is experiencing cognitive dissonance. The seller should reinforce the decision with reassurance warranty support and follow up communication to reduce doubt.
questions.explanation: Diagnose dissonance and propose reassurance measures.

questions.text: Explain the relationship between consumer behaviour and marketing strategy
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Consumer behaviour insights guide segmentation targeting positioning and the marketing mix ensuring products prices channels and promotion match consumer needs.
questions.explanation: Link consumer understanding to each element of strategy.

questions.text: Distinguish between high involvement and low involvement purchases
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: High involvement purchases are expensive risky and infrequent requiring deep evaluation while low involvement purchases are routine and need little thought.
questions.explanation: Risk and cost determine the level of involvement.

questions.text: The theory that consumers pass through innovators early adopters and laggards is the
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Diffusion theory classifies adopters by how quickly they accept innovations.

questions.text: Explain the factors that determine the level of consumer involvement
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Involvement depends on price risk self image social visibility and emotional appeal of the product with higher stakes producing higher involvement.
questions.explanation: Cover the product and situational factors raising involvement.

questions.text: A consumer buys the same brand habitually without evaluation. This is
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Routine response behaviour involves little search and habitual choice.

questions.text: Explain the psychological factors influencing consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Motivation perception learning and attitudes are the key psychological factors that drive and shape how consumers interpret and respond to marketing.
questions.explanation: Cover each psychological factor and its effect.

questions.text: The process of giving meaning to sensory stimuli is called perception
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Perception is selecting organising and interpreting stimuli into meaning.

questions.text: Explain the social factors influencing consumer behaviour
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Reference groups family roles and status and opinion leaders shape consumer choices by setting norms providing information and exerting pressure to conform.
questions.explanation: Cover reference groups family and opinion leaders.

questions.text: List the types of buying decisions
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Routine limited problem solving and extensive problem solving decisions.
questions.explanation: The types differ by the effort and risk involved.

questions.text: Explain the concept and determinants of lifestyle
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Lifestyle is a persons pattern of living expressed in activities interests and opinions and is shaped by culture social class and personality affecting consumption choices.
questions.explanation: Cover the AIO framework and its determinants.

questions.text: The group a person aspires to join is called an aspirational reference group
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.explanation: Aspirational groups are those the individual wishes to belong to.

questions.text: Explain the importance of consumer behaviour in service marketing
questions.subject: Consumer Behaviour
questions.topic: Nature and models of consumer behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Services are intangible and inseparable so understanding consumer expectations perceptions and satisfaction is essential to design and deliver quality service experiences.
questions.explanation: Link the special features of services to consumer understanding.
